title: Add R and Python examples to the imbalanced chapters
description:
Fills in the `R Examples` and `Python Examples` sections across all nine method chapters in the Imbalanced part. Only up-sampling and down-sampling had any examples before, and no chapter in the part had Python. Follows on from #70, which put the dependencies in place.

All the chapters share one data set, the two largest `MS_Zoning` classes of `ames` with numeric predictors, so the methods can be compared against each other. Most of them need numeric predictors and enough members per class to run a nearest neighbor search, which the full seven-class data does not provide.

Writing the examples surfaced several places where the two ecosystems disagree, and the chapters now document them rather than papering over them: themis and imblearn use different default neighbour counts for Near-Miss, which is invisible for versions 1 and 3 but moves version 2 a long way; SMOTE's interpolation is visible in themis and silently truncated by imblearn on integer columns; and edited nearest neighbors applies its rule to every class in themis but only the majority in imblearn.

Two chapters needed more than examples. The instance hardness chapter described only the model-based way of computing hardness, which is what imblearn does, while themis fits no model at all, so it has been reframed as a family with two estimation strategies. The SMOTE variants chapter had headings that skipped from `h1` to `h3`.

Three samplers are documented as limitations rather than shown running. `InstanceHardnessThreshold`, `NeighbourhoodCleaningRule` and `EditedNearestNeighbours(kind_sel="mode")` all error on non-numeric class labels at the currently pinned versions, which is a scipy incompatibility rather than anything about the methods, and each chapter says so.

The last commit is worth skipping in review. It holds five chapters outside this part whose output changes on every render regardless of content.

## Test plan

Full `quarto render` completes across all 146 chapters with no errors and no warnings rendered into output. Every example in this PR was checked against its rendered HTML rather than against a clean exit code, since `quarto render` exits 0 even when it reports `WARN: Error encountered when rendering files`.

title: Update dependencies for the imbalanced chapters
description:
Groundwork for adding R and Python examples to the imbalanced chapters, which currently have almost none. Neither ecosystem could run those examples before this: themis was a version behind the release that adds `step_cnn()`, `step_enn()`, and `step_instance_hardness()`, and imbalanced-learn was not a project dependency at all.

No chapter content changes here, deliberately, so that rendering churn caused by the upgrades stays separable from churn caused by the new examples in the follow-up PR.

Two knock-on upgrades were needed rather than optional. Taking imbalanced-learn unpinned brings scikit-learn to 1.8.0, which removed the private `BaseEstimator._get_tags()` API that category-encoders 2.6.3 still called; without that bump the render aborts at `categorical-binary.qmd`. feature-engine was updated in the same spirit rather than left on a stale pin.

The re-render diff is almost entirely scikit-learn 1.8's estimator HTML repr, which swapped its `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` blocks for explicit `.light`/`.dark` classes. The one substantive change is `imbalenced-upsample.html`, where themis 1.1.0 samples different rows; the resulting class counts are unchanged.

## Test plan

Full `quarto render` completes across all 146 chapters with no errors and no warnings rendered into output. Note that `quarto render` exits 0 even when it reports `WARN: Error encountered when rendering files`, so the log needs checking directly rather than trusting exit status.
